page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6a.2xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 4 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7H12 processor running at a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It operates on the x86_64 architecture and supports hardware features such as Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX), AES cryptography, and SHA instruction extensions. This instance does not include local NVMe storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals moderate performance characteristics with notable tradeoffs. The AMD EPYC 7H12 processor delivers average performance in Geekbench single-core (1315.0) and multi-core (5025.0) tests, as well as average results in software compilation (7237.0) and image processing (5127.0). However, raw compute benchmarks show limitations, with stress-ng single-core performance falling into the bottom 10% and multi-core performance categorized as weak. Memory bandwidth also exhibits a sharp contrast: cached small-block reads achieve an average throughput of 395.92 GB/sec, whereas uncached large-block reads and writes drop to a weak 32.16 GB/sec and 16.75 GB/sec, respectively.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.c6a.2xlarge offers a dedicated compute profile with a lower memory-to-vCPU ratio, making it a resource-dense option for workloads that do not require massive RAM allocations. Given the average performance in static web serving (6.78 GB/sec) and database operations, but weaker performance in high-throughput Redis SET operations, this instance is best suited for moderate web serving, software compilation, and general-purpose compute tasks that fit within its 16.0 GB memory envelope.

It operates on the x86_64 architecture with a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and lacks local storage or GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks indicate average capabilities in Geekbench multi-core, software compilation, and static web serving, though raw stress-ng CPU tests and uncached memory bandwidth show weaker results. Qualitatively, the instance provides a cost-effective dedicated compute resource for workloads with modest memory requirements. It is best suited for moderate web serving, software compilation, and general-purpose compute tasks.
